paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא רָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽלְדָה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַתְּקַנֵּ֥א רָחֵ֖ל בַּאֲחֹתָ֑הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ הָֽבָה־לִּ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְאִם־אַ֖יִן מֵתָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי׃

i18n.en: And when Rachel saw that she bore Ya'aqov no children, Rachel envied her sister; and she said to Ya'aqov, Give me children, or else I die.

paragraphs.commentary:
Rachel's *havah-li banim v-im ayin meta anokhi* — *Give me children, or else I die* — is the chapter's opening force, and the most-condensed feminine reproductive-anguish formula in the patriarchal corpus. The imperative *havah* (from *yahav*, *give*) is rare and emphatic — the same form deployed at the human-collective summons in the Babel narrative (*havah nilbenah*, Gen 11:3; *havah neredah*, Gen 11:7, in the Elohim's deliberative speech). The intertextual echo positions Rachel's cry in implicit-parallel to the foundational *havah*-formulae of Gen 11. Standard English (ASV/KJV) smooths the imperative force to *give me children*; the WoH preserves the ASV-baseline phrasing while flagging the *havah*-cluster in the glossary apparatus.

The barren-wife cry-to-husband motif has a sharp comparative parallel at 1 Sam 1:8-15 (Hannah's anguish at Shiloh), where the husband Elkanah's response is consolation (*am I not better to you than ten sons?*) — Ya'aqov's response here (v 2) is rebuke (*am I in the place of Elohim?*). The contrast is structural: the Genesis matriarch-cry receives a husband-rebuke; the prophetic-mother-cry receives a husband-consolation. Sarna (*JPS* p. 208) and Westermann (*Genesis 12-36* pp. 472-473) read the contrast as deliberate.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּרָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲתַ֤חַת אֱלֹהִים֙ אָנֹ֔כִי אֲשֶׁר־מָנַ֥ע מִמֵּ֖ךְ פְּרִי־בָֽטֶן׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov's anger was kindled against Rachel; and he said, Am I in the place of Elohim, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְתֵלֵד֙ עַל־בִּרְכַּ֔י וְאִבָּנֶ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And she said, Behold, my handmaid Bilhah, go in to her; and she shall bear upon my knees, and I also shall be built up through her.

paragraphs.commentary: Rachel's offering of Bilhah replays the Gen 16 Sarai-Hagar arrangement almost verbatim: the barren wife gives her *shifchah* to the husband *l-ishah*, and the substitute-wife's children count legally as the mistress's. The *al-birkai* (*upon my knees*) idiom marks the ANE adoption-formula: the receiving-on-the-knees of the new-born ratifies the legal-mother's claim (compare Gen 50:23, Job 3:12; Speiser AB p. 230 cites the Hurrian-Nuzi parallels). *V-ibaneh gam-anokhi mimenah* — *and I also shall be built up through her* — puns on *banah* (build) / *ben* (son): the wife is *built-up-with-sons* through her substitute. The institutional background is documented at the [shifchah-substitute-wife-arrangement](#shifchah-substitute-wife-arrangement) glossary entry.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֥ה שִׁפְחָתָ֖הּ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife; and Ya'aqov went in to her.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֣הַר בִּלְהָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And Bilhah conceived, and bore Ya'aqov a son.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ דָּנַ֣נִּי אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְגַם֙ שָׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֔י וַיִּתֶּן־לִ֖י בֵּ֑ן עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ דָּֽן׃

i18n.en: And Rachel said, Elohim has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son; therefore she called his name Dan.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Dan name-aetiology** — *dananni Elohim* (*Elohim has judged me*) on the root *dyn / din* (*judge, vindicate, plead a cause*). The verb here carries the forensic-vindication sense: Rachel reads Bilhah's son as Elohim's *verdict* in her favor against Le'ah — the barrenness-suit has been adjudicated. The same root nominalized produces *Dan* (*he-has-judged / judge*). The naming-pattern shifts from Gen 29's Le'ah-births: where Le'ah anchored her sons' names on YHWH-as-the-perceiver (*ra'ah*, *shama*) and on her relational-position (*lavah*), Rachel anchors Dan's name on a forensic verdict — the sister-rivalry has reached the divine-court.

Downstream: the tribal-blessing at Gen 49:16 reactivates the etymology — *Dan yadin amo* (*Dan shall judge his people*) — playing on the same root. Bare *Elohim* (no article) is preserved per the name-like-subject convention used at Gen 21:2, 22:1.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֣הַר ע֔וֹד וַתֵּ֕לֶד בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֑ל בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Bilhah Rachel's handmaid conceived again, and bore Ya'aqov a second son.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל נַפְתּוּלֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֧ים ׀ נִפְתַּ֛לְתִּי עִם־אֲחֹתִ֖י גַּם־יָכֹ֑לְתִּי וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ נַפְתָּלִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Rachel said, With mighty wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and have prevailed; and she called his name Naphtali.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Naphtali name-aetiology** — *naftulei Elohim niftalti im-achoti gam-yakholti* — a doubly-cognate verb-and-noun construction (the rare *naftulim* nominalization paired with finite-verb *niftalti*) anchoring the name *Naftali* on the root *p-t-l* (*twist, wrestle, contend*).

The philological crux is the genitive *Elohim*. Two readings have been defended: **(a) superlative-Elohim** — *mighty wrestlings* — treating *Elohim* as the intensifying-attributive idiom paralleled at *har'rei El* (*mountains of El* = *mighty mountains*, Ps 36:7) and *nasi Elohim* (*a prince of God* = *a mighty prince*, Gen 23:6); **(b) genitive-divine** — *wrestlings of Elohim*, i.e. Elohim-given or Elohim-mediated contests, Rachel claiming divine alliance against Le'ah. ASV/KJV follow (a); Alter (*Five Books of Moses* 2004), Speiser (*AB Genesis* 1964), and the JPS lean toward (a-modified) — *fateful contest*. The WoH preserves the ASV-baseline *mighty wrestlings* but flags the dispute here. The choice is theologically-non-trivial: reading (a) magnifies the contest's intensity; reading (b) makes Rachel a litigant claiming the divine-side.

*Gam-yakholti* (*and I have prevailed*) is forensic-victory language — Rachel reads Naphtali's birth as a courtroom-win, structurally paired with Dan's *dananni Elohim* (the verdict, v 6). The two Bilhah-sons are framed as **judgment-and-victory** in the sister-rivalry.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא לֵאָ֔ה כִּ֥י עָמְדָ֖ה מִלֶּ֑דֶת וַתִּקַּח֙ אֶת־זִלְפָּ֣ה שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: When Le'ah saw that she had left off bearing, she took Zilpah her handmaid, and gave her to Ya'aqov to wife.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֥ב בֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And Zilpah Le'ah's handmaid bore Ya'aqov a son.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לֵאָ֖ה בגד [בָּ֣א] [גָ֑ד] וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ גָּֽד׃

i18n.en: And Le'ah said, Fortune has come! and she called his name Gad.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Gad name-aetiology — the ketiv/qere crux.** The consonantal text (ketiv) reads בגד as a single word *b'gad* (*with fortune* / *by good luck*; preposition + noun); the Masoretic vocalization (qere) reads it as two words *ba gad* (*Fortune has come!*; perfect-verb 3ms *ba* + noun *gad*). The qere is the more etymologically-transparent reading for the tribal-name. The WoH follows the qere per the project's conservative rabbinic-reading-tradition default.

*Gad* itself is a loaded noun in HB-comparative-philology: it is the name of a **Canaanite-Aramean fortune-deity** (attested in Phoenician inscriptions as **GD**, in the Northwest Semitic onomasticon, and at Isa 65:11 as a YHWH-rejected fortune-deity whose worship was a post-exilic-syncretism-problem — *ha-orkhim la-Gad shulchan* — *those who set a table for Gad*). The Le'ah-naming-speech here does not name the deity; it deploys the noun in its appellative sense (*fortune*) on the conventional Israelite reading. Whether the underlying tradition preserves a fossilized-deity-name pun is a comparative-religion question the rabbinic-tradition deliberately suppressed by the qere's verbal-clause re-parsing. Cross *editor-report.md* for further notes.

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת לֵאָ֔ה בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Zilpah Le'ah's handmaid bore Ya'aqov a second son.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֔ה בְּאָשְׁרִ֕י כִּ֥י אִשְּׁר֖וּנִי בָּנ֑וֹת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אָשֵֽׁר׃

i18n.en: And Le'ah said, In my happiness! for the daughters will call me blessed; and she called his name Asher.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Asher name-aetiology** — the doubled-anchor pun *b-oshri* (*in my happiness/good-fortune*, noun *osher*) and *ish'runi banot* (*the daughters will call me blessed/happy*, verb *asher* in the piel, *to declare blessed*). The two cognate-anchors converge on the name *Asher* (*the blessed-one / fortunate-one*). The verb-noun-name triplet *osher / asher / Asher* compresses three cognate-derivations into a single utterance.

The *banot* (*daughters*) is the marriage-praise-genre marker: it is the same chorus-formula found at Song 6:9 (*banot v-ya'shruha* — *the daughters... they pronounced her blessed*) and Prov 31:28 (*qamu vaneha va-y'ash'ruha* — *her children rose up and called her blessed*). Le'ah is voicing herself into the canonical-genre of woman-praise. Asher's name pairs with Gad's *fortune*-semantics: the two Zilpah-sons are framed as **the fortunate-pair**, matching Bilhah's *judgment-and-victory* pair (Dan/Naphtali).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֶל־לֵאָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל־לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי־נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And Re'uven went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Le'ah. Then Rachel said to Le'ah, Give me, I pray you, of your son's mandrakes.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The *duda'im* — mandrakes.** The plant *Mandragora officinarum* (autumnalis in the southern Levant) — a fleshy-rooted member of the Solanaceae bearing yellow-orange fruit at the wheat-harvest season (May-June), with documented psychoactive and aphrodisiac properties through tropane-alkaloid content (atropine, scopolamine). The *duda'im* appear in the HB only here (vv 14-16) and at Song 7:14 (*ha-duda'im natnu reach* — *the mandrakes give forth fragrance*) — both contexts attaching the plant to sexual / fertility / love-magic register. The Hebrew *duda'im* plays etymologically on *dod* (*beloved, love-making*) — both nouns share the d-w-d / d-d root — and the Song-of-Songs context confirms the love-magic semantic-field.

**ANE comparative.** The mandrake-as-aphrodisiac is documented across the ANE materia medica: Egyptian love-poetry (Papyrus Harris 500 lists *rrmt* / mandrake among love-charm botanicals); Mesopotamian medical lists; and Greek Theophrastus (*Hist. Plant.* 9.9.1) noting its conception-inducing reputation, picked up by Pliny (*Nat. Hist.* 25.94). Zohary (*Plants of the Bible* 1982, pp. 188-189) identifies the species and surveys the cross-cultural fertility-folklore.

**The narrative-irony.** Rachel — the loved-but-barren wife — bargains for the fertility-plant from Le'ah — the unloved-but-fertile wife — by trading her marital-night-rights. And yet the chapter does not credit the mandrakes for the conception that follows: at v 17 the narrator says *va-yishma Elohim el-Le'ah* (*and Elohim hearkened to Le'ah*) — it is Le'ah, not Rachel, who conceives next, and the conception is attributed to divine-hearing, not to the herbalism. The narrator's silence on the mandrakes' efficacy is itself a theological-comment: folk-fertility-magic and divine-fertility are juxtaposed without the text choosing.

The WoH renders *duda'im* as *mandrakes* (ASV-baseline botanical-traditional); the *dod*-etymology and ANE materia-medica apparatus is carried in the glossary entry.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת־אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת־דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And she said to her, Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband? and would you take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with you tonight for your son's mandrakes.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶרֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov came from the field in the evening, and Le'ah went out to meet him, and said, You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

paragraphs.commentary: Le'ah's *sakhor sekhartikha* (*I have surely hired you*) deploys the infinitive-absolute + finite-verb construction for emphasis, and seeds the *sakhar* (*hire, wages*) lexeme that will be retrieved two verses later in Yissakhar's name-aetiology (v 18). The mandrake-trade is reframed by Le'ah as a wage-transaction: Ya'aqov is *hired* for the night with botanical-currency, and his subsequent fifth-son-with-Le'ah is the *wages* of the deal.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־לֵאָ֑ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּ֥ן חֲמִישִֽׁי׃

i18n.en: And Elohim hearkened to Le'ah, and she conceived, and bore Ya'aqov a fifth son.

paragraphs.commentary: **The narrator does not credit the mandrakes for the conception.** The verse's structural-pivot is *va-yishma Elohim el-Le'ah* — *and Elohim hearkened to Le'ah* — repeating the *shama* (hear) verb that anchored Shim'on's earlier aetiology (Gen 29:33). The narrator deliberately substitutes the divine-hearing for the herbal-aphrodisiac as the operative cause. Folk-fertility-magic is recorded (vv 14-16 take it seriously enough to narrate the trade); the conception itself is credited elsewhere. The juxtaposition is the chapter's most-economical theological-statement on the relation between technique and providence — repeated later in compressed form at the rod-trick narrative (vv 37-42; cf. Gen 31:9-13 for the dream-revelation reframe).

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשָּׂשכָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Le'ah said, Elohim has given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband; and she called his name Yissakhar.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Yissakhar name-aetiology** — *natan Elohim sekhari* (*Elohim has given me my hire*) on the lexeme *sakhar* (*hire, wages*) that was already activated at v 16 (*sakhor sekhartikha*, Le'ah's mandrake-trade phrasing). The name itself (יִשָּׂשכָר) admits three philological-analyses: (a) *yesh sakhar* (*there is hire*); (b) *yissa sakhar* (*he carries hire*); (c) an older form *ish-sakar* (*man of hire*). The orthographic doubling of the second sin/shin in MT is itself a Masoretic preservation-crux, marking the name as morphologically-archaic.

Le'ah's transactional logic is doubly-ironic: she reads the fifth-son as *wages* for having earlier *given* her *shifchah* (the Zilpah-arrangement, v 9) — but the immediate-narrative-context credits the conception not to Zilpah's service but to the mandrake-trade and the divine-hearing (v 17). Three causal-frames overlap in a single naming-speech: the shifchah-service, the herbal-trade, and the divine-hearing. The WoH preserves the ASV-baseline *my hire* (the wages-formula's literal force).

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ לֵאָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּן־שִׁשִּׁ֖י לְּיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And Le'ah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Ya'aqov.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים ׀ אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒ הַפַּ֙עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ זְבֻלֽוּן׃

i18n.en: And Le'ah said, Elohim has endowed me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons; and she called his name Zevulun.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Zevulun name-aetiology — the doubled-pun.** A single naming-speech conjoins two distinct verbs to the single name *Zevulun*, both rare in Genesis:

**(1)** *zavad* (*to endow with a gift*) in *zevadani Elohim oti zeved tov* (*Elohim has endowed me with a good endowment/dowry*). The verb is attested only here in Genesis and carries a Phoenician-Aramaic dowry-register; *zeved* as a noun denotes marital-property given by the father or by the deity.

**(2)** *zaval* (*to dwell, exalt, prince*) in *yizbeleni ishi* (*my husband will dwell-with / honor me*). The root surfaces again in the **Ugaritic** epithet *zbl b'l* (*Prince Baal*) and in 1 Kgs 8:13 (Solomon's temple-dedication: *beit zevul* — *lofty house*).

The doubled-pun is unusual: Le'ah voices both etymologies in a single utterance, and the name *Zevulun* carries both senses simultaneously. Speiser (*AB Genesis* 1964, p. 230) reads the verse as preservation of two competing folk-etymologies fused by the redactor — a redactional-doublet preserved rather than choosing-between. The WoH renders both senses explicit: *endowed me with a good dowry* + *my husband dwell with me*.

paragraphs.text: וְאַחַ֖ר יָ֣לְדָה בַּ֑ת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמָ֖הּ דִּינָֽה׃

i18n.en: And afterwards she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Dinah — the absent aetiology.** The first named daughter in the Genesis cycle, and the only Jacob-child whose birth-notice is given **without** a folk-etymological naming-speech. The conspicuous absence is a redactional-deliberate marker: (a) Dinah is not a tribe — the tribal-eponym-system has no slot for her, so the aetiology that anchors brothers' names to their tribes' fates has nothing to anchor to; (b) the absence anticipates Dinah's central tragedy at Gen 34 (the Shechem episode), where her silence in her own narrative is the chapter's most-discussed feature (Sternberg *Poetics of Biblical Narrative* 1985 ch. 12; Fewell-Gunn *Tipping the Balance* 1991); (c) the name *Dinah* (דִּינָה) is itself a feminine-form of *dyn / din* (*judge*), echoing Dan's name (v 6) — the wordplay is technically present but unspoken; the Dan-Dinah judgment-pair frames the chapter's name-cluster.

The laconic notice is preserved verbatim (ASV-baseline). The aetiological-silence is itself the comment.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־רָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And Elohim remembered Rachel, and Elohim hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

paragraphs.commentary: The verse triple-deploys the HB's divine-fertility-formulae: *va-yizkor Elohim* (*and Elohim remembered* — the *zakhar* verb that marks each major-covenantal-inflection; cf. Gen 8:1 Noah, Gen 19:29 Lot, Exod 2:24 the Exodus prelude); *va-yishma eleha Elohim* (*and Elohim hearkened to her* — the *shama* verb that anchored Le'ah's earlier conceptions, vv 17; Shim'on 29:33); *va-yiftach et-rachmah* (*and opened her womb* — the *patach-rechem* formula matched at Gen 29:31 for Le'ah, and at 1 Sam 1 for Hannah). Three formulae compressed into a single verse mark Rachel's conception as the chapter's theological-climax: every divine-fertility-vocabulary the HB possesses is deployed at once.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אָסַ֥ף אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־חֶרְפָּתִֽי׃

i18n.en: And she conceived, and bore a son, and said, Elohim has taken away my reproach.

paragraphs.commentary:
**First Yosef aetiology — *asaf Elohim et-cherpati*** (*Elohim has taken away / gathered up my reproach*). The verb *asaf* (*gather up, remove, take in*) here in the rare *remove-as-shame-cleared* sense (1 Sam 25:39; Isa 4:1). The name *Yosef* is etymologically from *yasaf* (*add, increase*, v 24), but the narrator gives a **doubled aetiology** spread across two verses — *asaf* (v 23, past-perfective, closing the barrenness-chapter) and *yasaf* (v 24, precative-future, opening toward the next son). The two consonantal-roots *'-s-p* (*asaf*) and *y-s-p* (*yasaf*) overlap only at the central *s-p* — the wordplay is on near-homonymy rather than strict-cognate, and the narrator deliberately deploys both to give Yosef a doubled-name-anchor unique among the twelve sons.

*Cherpah* (*reproach, disgrace*) is the technical-term for the social-shame of barrenness; the lexeme threads the Sarah-Rachel-Hannah barrenness-typology (Gen 11:30 / 16:1-2 / 18:11-15; 1 Sam 1:6 *gam ka'asateh tzaratah*). Rachel reads Yosef's birth as the **lifting** of that shame.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקְרָ֧א אֶת־שְׁמ֛וֹ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר יֹסֵ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י בֵּ֥ן אַחֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And she called his name Yosef, saying, May YHWH add to me another son.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Second Yosef aetiology — *yosef YHWH li ben acher*** (*May YHWH add to me another son*). The name *Yosef* is here anchored on its true etymological root *yasaf* (*add, increase*; hiphil-jussive *yosef* *let-him-add*). Rachel's wish is precative-future: she names the present-son with reference to a son-not-yet-born, anticipating Benjamin (Gen 35:16-20; Rachel's death-birth, where she will name the son *Ben-Oni* — *son of my sorrow* — and Ya'aqov will rename him *Binyamin*, *son of the right hand*).

**The doublet's structure.** The two successive-verses give two etymologies: (v 23) *asaf* — past-perfective, backward-looking (the barrenness now closed); (v 24) *yasaf* — precative-future, forward-looking (the next son anticipated). The doublet is **unique** in the patriarchal name-aetiology corpus: no other tribal-name receives two etymologies in successive verses (Zevulun's doublet at v 20 is compressed into a single verse). The two-source documentary reading (Wellhausen-Friedman) attributes v 23 (asaf, *Elohim*-as-divine-name) and v 24 (yasaf, *YHWH*-as-divine-name) to different source-strands (E and J respectively) fused at the redactional level — Sarna *JPS* p. 213 surveys; Westermann *Genesis 12-36* pp. 478-479 reads the doublet as deliberate-final-form-marker rather than source-seam. **The narrative-effect is the same on either reading**: Yosef's birth is given the heaviest naming-apparatus of the twelve, marking him structurally as the central-son of the Joseph-cycle that will dominate Gen 37-50.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָלְדָ֥ה רָחֵ֖ל אֶת־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֙נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל־מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Yosef, that Ya'aqov said to Lavan, Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my country.

paragraphs.commentary: The departure-request is structurally hinged: Yosef's birth completes the seven-year-second-wage (Gen 29:30) **and** signals Ya'aqov's release from the Lavan-household. *Shallcheni v-elkhah el-mqomi u-l-artzi* (*send me away that I may go to my own place and to my country*) is the formal-leave-taking-formula, echoed at Gen 24:54-56 (Eliezer's request to Lavan, completing the Rebekah-arrangement) — the same Lavan, the same release-from-Aram-formula. Lavan's response (vv 27-34) re-opens the contract; the leave-taking will be deferred until Gen 31.

paragraphs.text: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת־נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת־יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת־עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם־נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ נִחַ֕שְׁתִּי וַיְבָרֲכֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְלָלֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And Lavan said to him, If now I have found favor in your eyes, tarry — I have divined that YHWH has blessed me for your sake.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Lavan's *nichashti* — the first patriarchal-narrative use of *nichesh*.** The Piel of *n-ch-sh* (*to practice divination, augury, hydromancy, ophiomancy*) is the technical-term for a class of ANE mantic-techniques: serpent-omens (the root is denominative from *nachash*, *serpent*), liver-divination (hepatoscopy), cup-divination (lecanomancy — cf. Gen 44:5, 15, Yosef's silver-cup), and other omen-reading. Lavan announces the means by which he learned of YHWH's blessing: a mantic-procedure, voiced positively, with no narrator-condemnation.

The lexeme later carries the weight of explicit-prohibition. **Lev 19:26** — *lo t'nachashu v-lo t'onenu* (*you shall not practice divination, and you shall not soothsay*). **Deut 18:10** — the diviner is listed among the abominations driving the Canaanites out. **2 Kgs 17:17** (the Northern Kingdom's apostasy-catalog) and **21:6** (Manasseh's cultic-crimes) both cite *nichesh* as a marker of YHWH-rejection. Lavan's casual deployment of the verb here positions him as a **practitioner of techniques the later-Israelite-tradition will explicitly prohibit** — matching his later characterization at Gen 31:19, 31:34-35 as a *teraphim*-owner (household-idols-keeper).

The ASV softens to *I have learned by experience* (treating *nichashti* as idiomatic-observational); KJV likewise *I have learned by experience*. Alter and Speiser preserve the technical-cultic force: *I have prospered by divination* / *I divine that*. The WoH follows Alter/Speiser and renders *I have divined* — the irony is the chapter's most-pointed: a pagan-divination-procedure correctly identifies YHWH's blessing on Ya'aqov. The Aramean-cultic-background of the Jacob-Lavan cycle is given a direct lexical-flag.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נָקְבָ֧ה שְׂכָרְךָ֛ עָלַ֖י וְאֶתֵּֽנָה׃

i18n.en: And he said, Appoint me your wages, and I will give it.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה מִקְנְךָ֖ אִתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, You know how I have served you, and how your cattle have fared with me.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ לְרַגְלִ֑י וְעַתָּ֗ה מָתַ֛י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה גַם־אָנֹכִ֖י לְבֵיתִֽי׃

i18n.en: For it was little that you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude; and YHWH has blessed you wherever I turned. And now when shall I provide for my own house also?

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yifrotz la-rov* (*and it has burst forth to a multitude*) seeds the *paratz*-verb that will fulfill itself at v 43 (*va-yifrotz ha-ish me'od me'od* — *and the man burst forth exceedingly, exceedingly*). The verb's eruptive-force is the chapter's quantitative-formula: small → multitude → exceedingly-exceedingly. The same root will name **Peretz** (Gen 38:29, Judah's son by Tamar) and **Baal-Peratzim** (2 Sam 5:20). See [paratz-me'od-prosperity-formula](#paratz-me'od-prosperity-formula).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מָ֣ה אֶתֶּן־לָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לֹא־תִתֶּן־לִ֣י מְא֔וּמָה אִם־תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And he said, What shall I give you? And Ya'aqov said, You shall not give me anything; if you will do this thing for me, I will again feed your flock and keep it:

paragraphs.text: אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר בְּכָל־צֹֽאנְךָ֜ הַיּ֗וֹם הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כָּל־שֶׂ֣ה ׀ נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכָל־שֶׂה־חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים וְהָיָ֖ה שְׂכָרִֽי׃

i18n.en: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and that shall be my wages.

paragraphs.text: וְעָֽנְתָה־בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי־תָב֥וֹא עַל־שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־אֵינֶנּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: So shall my righteousness answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my wages that is before you: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that, if found with me, shall be counted stolen.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן הֵ֑ן ל֖וּ יְהִ֥י כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And Lavan said, Behold, I would it were according to your word.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת־הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־לָבָן֙ בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־ח֖וּם בַּכְּשָׂבִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בְּיַד־בָּנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And he removed that day the he-goats that were ringstreaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן הַנּוֹתָרֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And he set three days' journey between himself and Ya'aqov; and Ya'aqov was feeding the rest of Lavan's flocks.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעֶרְמ֑וֹן וַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov took rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond, and of the plane-tree; and peeled white streaks in them, exposing the white which was in the rods.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The three rod-trees — the *lavan*-cluster.** The botanical-triad chosen here is **not** random: each species' name or natural-appearance reinforces the *whiteness* (*lavan*) at the verbal-and-visual core of the trick.

- **Livneh (לִבְנֶה)** — *poplar* (ASV/Vulgate *populus*), alternatively *storax/styrax* (Rashi, Ibn Ezra — citing the tree's medicinal-aromatic resin). The noun **literally encodes *lavan***: *l-b-n* is the white-color root; *livneh* is *the-white-tree*. Westermann notes the etymology is transparent.
- **Luz (לוּז)** — *almond* (ASV/Vulgate *amygdalus*), alternatively *hazel* (KJV). The almond's bark, when peeled, exposes characteristically-white inner-wood — the peeling-procedure itself activates the color.
- **Ermon (עֶרְמוֹן)** — *plane-tree* (*Platanus orientalis*). The plane-tree's defining feature is **piebald bark that sheds in white patches** — the tree's natural appearance is already *speckled / spotted / ringstreaked*, the very pattern Ya'aqov wants the flocks to produce.

**The Lavan / livneh pun.** *Ya'aqov takes lvn-rods* (*livneh* + the *l-b-n* exposed-white) **to outsmart Lavan** (לָבָן — *the White One*). The wordplay is the chapter's most-pointed: *Lavan* the man is undone by *lavan* the color through *livneh* the tree. Westermann (*Genesis 12-36* pp. 484-486), Alter (*Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 161), and Sarna (*JPS* p. 215) all flag the cluster.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת־הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרֳהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקֲת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן וַיֵּחַ֖מְנָה בְּבֹאָ֥ן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And he set the rods which he had peeled before the flocks in the gutters in the watering-troughs where the flocks came to drink; and they conceived when they came to drink.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The rod-trick as sympathetic-fertility magic.** The mechanism narrated at vv 37-42 — peeled white-streaked rods set at the watering-troughs at conception-time, producing speckled-spotted-ringstreaked offspring — is the most-explicit instance of **sympathetic / maternal-impression magic** in the patriarchal cycle, and arguably in the Pentateuch. The principle (what the pregnant animal sees at conception affects the offspring's coloration) is documented across the ANE breeding-tradition: Westermann (*Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 484-487) reads the trick as folk-veterinary-magic embedded in the source-tradition; Speiser (*AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 235-237) cites Mesopotamian veterinary-omen-texts — esp. the **Sumerian-Akkadian *šumma izbu* omen-series** (the *if-a-birth* anomaly-catalog), which includes maternal-impression entries; the same principle later disputed by Pliny (*Nat. Hist.* 7.51) and Aristotle (*Hist. Anim.* 7.6) and preserved through Western maternal-impression folklore into the modern period (Albright *From the Stone Age to Christianity* 1957 surveys).

**The technique-versus-providence doublet.** Within the patriarchal narrative the rod-trick is given **two competing causal-attributions** that the redactor preserves without choosing:

- **Here (Gen 30:37-42)** — the trick is Ya'aqov's *techne*. He **takes** rods, he **peels** them, he **sets** them, and the flocks conceive *al ha-maqlot* (*toward the rods*). The narrator gives no divine-causation in this passage.
- **Gen 31:9-13** — Ya'aqov retrospectively reframes the same events in a dream-revelation-speech to Rachel and Le'ah: *the elohim* showed him in a dream that the rams mounting the flocks were ringstreaked-speckled-grizzled, *because the elohim has taken away the cattle of your father and given them to me*. Sympathetic-magic is reframed as divine-providence.

The doublet is the same theological-structure as the mandrake-narrative earlier in the chapter (vv 14-17): folk-fertility-technique and divine-fertility-causation are juxtaposed without the text choosing between. The WoH preserves both etiologies; cross *editor-report.md* for the speculative-extension question.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּחֱמ֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן אֶל־הַמַּקְל֑וֹת וַתֵּלַ֣דְןָ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּטְלֻאִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks brought forth ringstreaked, speckled, and spotted.

paragraphs.text: וְהַכְּשָׂבִים֮ הִפְרִ֣יד יַעֲקֹב֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל־עָקֹ֛ד וְכָל־ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן וַיָּֽשֶׁת־ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל־צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstreaked and all the black in the flock of Lavan; and he put his own droves apart, and put them not unto Lavan's flock.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּכָל־יַחֵם֮ הַצֹּ֣אן הַמְקֻשָּׁרוֹת֒ וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת־הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרֳהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, whenever the stronger of the flock did conceive, that Ya'aqov laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods;

paragraphs.text: וּבְהַעֲטִ֥יף הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה הָעֲטֻפִים֙ לְלָבָ֔ן וְהַקְּשֻׁרִ֖ים לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

i18n.en: but when the flock were feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler were Lavan's, and the stronger Ya'aqov's.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְרֹ֥ץ הָאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, and handmaids and menservants, and camels and donkeys.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The *paratz me'od me'od* prosperity-formula.** *Va-yifrotz ha-ish me'od me'od* — *and the man burst forth exceedingly, exceedingly*. The verb *paratz* (*break forth, burst out, increase explosively*) doubled with the rare hyperbolic-intensive *me'od me'od* marks Ya'aqov's enrichment as **exceeding all prior measures**. The same verb at Gen 28:14 (the Bethel-ladder-dream: *u-faratzta yamah va-qedmah v-tzafonah va-negbah* — *you shall break forth to the west and east and north and south*) is **structurally fulfilled** here: the Bethel-promise within the chapter-arc is realized in the rod-trick's flock-increase.

The formula reaches further: at Exod 1:7 the same *paratz* anchors Israel's multiplication in Egypt (*va-yifru va-yishretzu va-yirbu va-ya'atzmu bi-me'od me'od*) — Pharaoh's threat-trigger. The verbal-noun *peretz* names Judah's son (Gen 38:29, the breach-birth); the cult-toponym *Baal-Peratzim* (2 Sam 5:20) names a place by the same root. The doubled *me'od* is rare (the intensifier is intensive-by-itself; the doubling is hyperbolic). The WoH preserves the ASV-baseline *increased exceedingly* in the running English; the doubled-*me'od* and *paratz*-cluster are flagged in the glossary apparatus.
